detailed_description: The JavaScript Obfuscator applies simple browser-side transformations to pasted JavaScript code. You can enable or disable variable/function renaming, string hex encoding, unicode wrapper escaping, dead-code injection, and a simplified control-flow wrapper, then click Obfuscate to generate output. The tool also includes a sample snippet and a copy button for the generated code. It is a lightweight experiment helper and does not provide cryptographic protection, AST-level rewriting, anti-debugging guarantees, or protection for secrets embedded in client-side code.
usage_steps: Paste JavaScript code into the input textarea or click Load Sample.
Choose the available checkbox options such as variable renaming, string encoding, unicode escape, dead-code injection, or control-flow flattening.
Click Obfuscate to generate the transformed code.
Review the output textarea and copy the result when needed.
usage_examples: Example 1: Try variable renaming on a small demo function and compare the output.
Example 2: Encode string literals in a copied snippet before using it in a quick prototype.
Example 3: Load the sample code to see how the available transformations change the text.
Example 4: Copy the transformed output for a local experiment while keeping important secrets out of client-side code.
